# Security and access control

<!-- docsync:auto:begin - generated by docsync, edits inside this block are overwritten -->
> **Section status: CURRENT** - reviewed 2026-11-24; covers 26 files (globs in the front matter).
<!-- docsync:auto:end -->

## Authentication
- **Users** sign in at `/login` (`POST /api/auth/login`) with email and password; **admins** at `/admin/login` (`POST /api/admin/auth/login`).
- **Passwords:** argon2 (`argon2-cffi`), with a password policy enforced on set.
- **Lockout:** after `AUTH_MAX_FAILED_LOGINS` (5) for `AUTH_LOCKOUT_MINUTES` (15). There is also a per-IP limit (`AUTH_IP_ATTEMPTS` 30 per 5 min).
- **Sessions:**
  - server-side rows in `auth_sessions`, referenced by an opaque public id in an httpOnly cookie: `mdat_session` (users) or `mdat_admin` (admins);
  - SameSite=Lax; Secure in `auto` mode over HTTPS;
  - user idle 720 min, maximum 168 h; admin idle 30 min, maximum 12 h;
  - users can see and revoke their sessions, or sign out everywhere.
- **Nothing is stored in localStorage for auth;** the browser cannot read the cookie.
- **Invites and password resets:**
  - one-time tokens in `auth_tokens` (invite 7 days, reset 24 hours), issued by admins and copied by hand (no email);
  - new and reset admins and bootstrap admins must change their password at first sign-in.
- **Recovery:** `python -m app.auth.cli create-admin | list-admins | unlock`.

## Authorisation
| Role / permission | Can do | Enforced in |
|---|---|---|
| Platform admin (separate account) | Workspaces and their keys, users, memberships, roles, admins, the audit log, health, cross-workspace logs, Settings writes, Cleanup, vault `rotate-key` and `generate-key`. No workspace data permissions. | `auth/middleware.py` (ADMIN rules), `routes/admin.py` |
| maintainer | All 26 permissions | `auth/permissions.py` rules, checked by the middleware; mirrored in the UI by `lib/policy.tsx` |
| builder | All `.view`, plus orchestrator.use, chat.use, agents.manage, tools.manage, workflows.run, workflows.manage, connectors.manage, knowledge.manage, vault.manage | Same |
| operator | All `.view`, plus chat.use, workflows.run | Same |
| reviewer | All `.view`, plus reviews.decide | Same |
| viewer | All `.view` | Same |
| `vault.reveal` | Reveal a secret value (also requires `VAULT_ALLOW_REVEAL`) | `routes/vault.py`, `vault/guard.py` |
| `workflows.deploy` | Publish, register and export workflows; deployment packages | Route rules |
| `catalog.*`, `rules.*`, `settings.view` (marked "shared") | Platform-wide data: every workspace sees and edits the same catalog and rules | Route rules; the tables are not scoped |

Unmatched routes are denied. Writes must also pass the same-site Origin check.

## Tenancy / isolation
- **A workspace equals one Mistral API key.** All Mistral-side data (agents, libraries, conversations, connectors, workflows, traces) is naturally separated by the key used for the call. The client is chosen per request from the active workspace (`dependencies.get_mistral_client`).
- **Local tables are scoped by `workspace_id`,** filtered automatically by `auth/scoping.py` (`with_loader_criteria` on select, update and delete; stamped on insert):
  - workflow_definitions, deleted_workflows, workflow_revisions, workflow_versions;
  - pipeline_runs, human_reviews, local_executions;
  - vault_secrets, vault_audit;
  - remote_servers, remote_deployments.
- **`build_lessons`** carries `workspace_id`, filtered in code.
- **Shared on purpose (platform-wide):**
  - the catalog (`ontology_*`, `industry_knowledge`);
  - knowledge items and sources;
  - process documents and templates;
  - rules and rule categories;
  - tool-safety rules;
  - `rag_*` tables (keyed by library id, which is workspace-specific at Mistral);
  - the Tool Service registry (all tools are shared across workspaces).
- **Shared, probably not intended** (see the known issues): `workflow_input_*`, and `remote_provider_accounts` plus the host-wide Brev login.
- **Raw SQL** (`text()` queries) bypasses the automatic filter and must add `workspace_id` itself. `count_rows(ws)` blocks deleting a workspace that still owns data.
- **Workers** run one process per workspace with only that workspace's key in their environment.

## Untrusted code and content
- **Generated code:**
  - the R2 policy gate (backend) screens the need;
  - then, in the Tool Service: the static policy (allowed and forbidden modules, AST checks), the tool-safety rules, ruff, and tests in a sandbox subprocess as `sandboxuser`, with `SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` 20 and `SANDBOX_MEMORY_MB` 512;
  - tools with write or delete side effects need approval (`review_required`).
  - **Gap:** approved code executes in-process in the Tool Service.
- **Expressions** in workflow conditions and transforms run in `expression_sandbox.py` (a restricted evaluator), not Python `eval`. The legacy native `calculate` tool does use `eval`.
- **Uploads:**
  - size limits (20 MB uploads, 25 MB knowledge sources, 512 KB process documents);
  - stored under generated names; served only to signed-in users;
  - converted by Mistral OCR or transcription, never executed.
- **Prompt injection:**
  - model output is always parsed as data and validated against schemas;
  - rules are enforced in code at creation and at run time (`rules/runtime.py`), not only in prompts;
  - human-review steps can gate risky actions;
  - guardrails (Mistral moderation) can be configured on agents and workflows.
  - There is no dedicated injection classifier.
- **LLM-produced workflow definitions** pass `validation.py` and dry runs before they are saved as verified.

## Secrets handling
- **At rest:**
  - vault values are Fernet-encrypted with `MultiFernet` (`VAULT_MASTER_KEYS`, newest first, or the generated `backend/vault_key.secret`);
  - each ciphertext is bound to its entry id and version (`{"v", "id", "n"}`) and checked on decrypt;
  - workspace Mistral keys use the same keys;
  - remote-server and provider credentials use a separate Fernet key (`REMOTE_SERVER_SECRET_KEY` or `backend/remote_servers_key.secret`).
- **Rotation:** add a new master key first, then `POST /api/vault/rotate-key` re-encrypts every value and kept version and reports what it could not read. Five versions are kept per secret.
- **Use:**
  - values are resolved only for allowed consumers (`allowed_consumers`), audited (`vault_audit`, 180 days), and never listed;
  - reveal needs `vault.reveal` and `VAULT_ALLOW_REVEAL`;
  - builds pass `vault:<ref>` references, never values.
- **Never logged or exported:**
  - secret values (scrubbed from tool results by `vault/redact.py` when `VAULT_REDACT_RESULTS`);
  - auth and admin request bodies (never traced);
  - password hashes and tokens;
  - trace attributes are redacted (`OBSERVABILITY_REDACT`) and capped at 16000 chars.
- **Files that must never be committed:** `.env`, `*.secret` and the databases (`.gitignore` and `.dockerignore` cover them).
